Pilot report: are LIONESS personal networks personal?

A review document: the pilot, its results, the spec, and the decisions log

Published

November 16, 2026

Summary

Scope. This document reports the pilot1 of the re-scoped project (proposal.md, final 2026-11-16): whether LIONESS personal networks are personal, that is, stable over repeated visits of the same person, able to identify her, and predictive of her next disease activity, and how much of each is the interferon level and the blood-cell mix. It was built from project-spec.md, decisions.md, and the saved results in pilot-d/results/; every number is computed from those files when the document renders.

Status. In STATUS.md the pilot is marked piloted-close-call2. Every clause the rule names as deciding passed: edges equal their formula, the fix removes the interferon part of edge stability, and the fix keeps a real personal network. The interferon part was smaller than the thresholds, identification barely depended on it, and edges carried no signal of the next visit’s activity.

Pilot question Answer Key evidence
1. Does the effect exist, and do edges equal their formula? fail and pass Excess stability of interferon pairs 0.064 (MCSE 0.0015) at very stable interferon; raw and first-order stability differed by -0.000117 to 0.000039 across all cells and pair groups.
2. Large enough at the measured interferon stability? fail and fail Excess 0.016 (MCSE 0.0009); identification on interferon pairs fell by 0.004 (MCSE 0.0014) with the fix.
3. Is there a fix, and do edges predict? pass, pass, fail Fixed excess 0.0019 to 0.0068; the fix kept the real module (0.0186 (MCSE 0.0004)); edges over genes for next-visit activity -0.0006 (MCSE 0.0009).

What needs your decision (details in Action items and limitations): the status call, and whether the paper’s message becomes the low reliability of single-sample edges (decisions log, D2 and D3) rather than an interferon-driven stability.

The idea

In plain language

LIONESS3 gives every blood sample a value for every pair of genes, an edge, and the set of edges is read as that person’s own network. If it is truly hers, it should look much the same when her blood is drawn again three months later, and it should pick her out from other people. An edge is almost exactly the product of the person’s two standardized gene levels, so anything stable about her, such as a steady interferon4 level or her own typical gene levels, makes her edges look stable, whether or not her genes work together in a personal way. Suppose a child’s interferon genes always sit 1 unit above average: their product is about 1 at every visit, so the edge “repeats”, although nothing about coordination is personal. This pilot simulates 131 children with six visits each, at the interferon stability measured in real children with lupus, and asks how stable edges are, how much of it is interferon, whether a corrected edge removes that part and keeps a real personal network, and whether edges predict the next visit’s disease activity.

Potential impact

LIONESS is used to give each person a network (M. L. Kuijjer et al. 2019; Marieke L. Kuijjer et al. 2019), and its reproducibility has been checked across reference sets but not across repeated samples of the same person. Blood gene expression is known to be partly person-specific (Whitney et al. 2003; Mishra et al. 2026), the lupus interferon signature is stable within patients (Petri et al. 2019), and cell composition drives much bulk co-expression (Farahbod and Pavlidis 2020); networks have been used to identify people from brain scans (Finn et al. 2015).

The pilot shows that single-sample edges are unreliable over visits: their stability ranged over 0.07 to 0.22 (Table 3), so one visit’s network says little about the next. What stability they have is mostly the person’s own gene levels; interferon pairs became about twice as stable when interferon was stable (0.069 to 0.144), but the pre-registered excess over cross pairs was only 0.016 (MCSE 0.0009). The first-order formula reproduces every edge’s stability exactly, and the corrected edges remove the interferon part while keeping a real personal module (Figure 4). For a user, the message is that a personal network is a poor biomarker on its own, and that its apparent personality is largely what the gene levels already carry.

Application: the study behind the data

The study

The data come from a longitudinal study of children with systemic lupus erythematosus5 (Banchereau et al. 2016), https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2016.03.008, GEO series GSE653916: whole-blood transcriptomes at repeated visits, with disease activity (SLEDAI) and measured blood-cell counts at every visit, and healthy children for comparison. The study reported a prevalent interferon signature, a plasmablast signature tracking activity, and neutrophil enrichment toward active nephritis. Table 1 gives the sizes and the within-child stability measured in this project.

Why the stability of edges

The quantity is the intraclass correlation of each edge over a person’s visits: the share of its variation that is between people rather than within a person over time. A personal network needs a high value; a value that comes from interferon or from the person’s gene levels is not network information.

Did the original study compute it?

No. The original study analysed gene modules with mixed models and stratified patients; it built no single-sample networks and measured no stability of edges.

In symbols

The person’s IFN factor (\(F_{wv}\) at visit \(v\) of person \(w\), with within-person intraclass correlation \(\kappa\)), the standardized expression (\(z\)), and the reference correlation (\(r\)) determine the edge and the stability its factor part inherits:

\[ \begin{aligned} e_{wv} &= r + z_{wvi} z_{wvj} - \frac{r}{2}\left(z_{wvi}^2 + z_{wvj}^2\right) + O_p\left(N^{-1}\right), \\ \mathrm{E}\left[e_{wv} \mid F_{wv}\right] &= \text{const} + \left[\lambda_i \lambda_j - \frac{r}{2}\left(\lambda_i^2 + \lambda_j^2\right)\right] F_{wv}^2, \\ \mathrm{ICC}\left(F^2\right) &= \kappa^2 . \end{aligned} \]

Symbol Meaning
\(F_{wv}\), \(\kappa\) IFN factor of person \(w\) at visit \(v\); its within-person intraclass correlation
\(z_{wvi}\) expression of gene \(i\), standardized by the reference
\(e_{wv}\) LIONESS edge of the pair \((i, j)\) for that sample
\(\mathrm{ICC}\) intraclass correlation over visits

The target is the stability of a person’s own co-expression; the computable quantity, the stability of her edges, adds the factor part (stable to \(\kappa^2\) times its share of the edge’s variance) and the part from her stable gene levels.

Critiquing the model

Any model is a simplification, and the useful question is not whether it is true but where it bends and whether the bend matters for the question being asked. The model above was chosen so that the problem could be written as a formula and checked by simulation, and each simplification that made that possible is a place where real data may behave differently. The table lists the main ones. Work through it one row at a time. The first column names the feature and the symbols in the equations that carry it, so find them there first. Then decide in your own words how the feature could fail for real data before reading the second column, and finally read the third column for what should be done to check it. Several of these checks are natural first tasks for the project. Which of them the pilot examined, and which it left open, is for you to find when you read the Methods and Results that follow.

Feature of the model Why it may not be realistic What should be done to check it
One IFN factor, stability \(\kappa_F\) the same for everyone Some children change IFN a lot, others not at all Let \(\kappa_F\) vary by person, from the data
Person gene levels of variance 0.5, independent across genes Real person-level differences are correlated across genes Estimate them from GSE65391
Six equally spaced visits Real visits are irregular, two to 22 per child Mirror each child’s visits
A personal module of spread 0.25 The size of real personal co-expression is unknown Vary it; estimate from data
Activity linked to one module through a smooth curve Real flares may change many genes abruptly Simulate flares as rare large changes
Normal noise Array data have heavier tails Resample residuals from the data

Methods

Design

The pilot simulates 131 people with repeated visits in 6 cells. Fifty genes: genes 1 to 20 follow the IFN factor (score: genes 1 to 5), genes 31 to 50 follow an observed cell-mix factor, and genes 21 to 30 form a module whose correlation may be personal or change with activity. Every gene carries the person’s own level. Edges are computed on all samples; each edge’s intraclass correlation over visits and fingerprinting accuracy are measured for raw, first-order, and partial-correlation edges; in three cells, six models predict the next visit’s activity with folds by person7.

Part Cells Main factors Replicates
A, B 1 to 6 IFN stability 0, 0.55, 0.9; module 0 or 0.25; 6 or 3 visits 200 per cell
C 1, 2, 6 activity unrelated or changing the module 200 per cell

The edge types are raw LIONESS edges, first-order edges (the one-line formula), and partial-correlation LIONESS edges given the IFN score and the observed cell mix (the fix). The prediction models are those of the first project, fitted by elastic net8 and scored by the concordance index9.

Known-answer checks

Known-answer checks come before any result, because every later number is only as good as the simulation that produced it. Each check sets up a case where the correct answer is known from theory, runs the simulation code on it, and compares the two. Agreement says nothing about the scientific question or about real data. It says that the code does what the model says. Disagreement means stopping to look for a bug before reading anything else, and the same checks apply to any code you write for the project.

Read each row of the table in four steps: the setting that was simulated, the known answer for that setting, what the simulation gave, and whether the gap between the two is small compared with the Monte Carlo standard error (MCSE). The MCSE is how much a simulated result moves from run to run because only a finite number of replicates was used. A gap within about two MCSE is noise, and a gap of several MCSE is a problem.

1 of 4 rows with a standard error are more than 2 MCSE from the known value.

Results

How to read the outputs

Each output traces back to a row of the design diagram (the captions name the part where one applies). Read each in the same four steps. First, find its row in the diagram, which says what was simulated and what was varied. Second, work out what one point or one table entry is, usually one combination of the varied factors, averaged over replicates. Third, identify the reference value that would hold if nothing were wrong, shown as a dashed or grey line wherever possible. Fourth, look for where the results leave that reference, and for which settings they do. The outputs report three kinds of quantity.

  • Bias is the average of an estimate minus its true value. When the truth is no difference, any average difference from 0 is a spurious difference created by the problem under study.
  • Level is how often a test rejects when there is truly nothing to find. A correct test at 0.05 rejects 5% of the time, so a rate above 0.05 means too many false alarms.
  • Power is how often a test rejects when there is a real effect. More is better, but only when the level is not inflated, because a test that rejects too often also looks powerful.

All rates and averages come from simulation, so each carries Monte Carlo error. That is why the figures show bars or a grey band, and why small differences should not be over-read.

This pilot reports intraclass correlations (0 when an edge changes completely between visits, 1 when it never changes), their excess over cross pairs, the share of people identified (chance is 1 in 131), and concordance (0.5 is chance).

Stability

Figure guide (part A). Each panel is one pair group; each row one cell. Red points are raw edges, purple first-order edges, blue the fix; the value is the excess stability over cross pairs, and the dashed line is no excess. Look for: whether red and purple points coincide everywhere; whether the red IFN points move right as IFN stability rises (cells 1, 2, 3) and the blue ones stay at the line; whether the blue module points move right in cells 4 and 5.

Identification

Figure guide (part B). As above, with the share of people identified from one other visit. Look for: how far above chance (under 0.01) the points sit, and whether the fix changes them.

Numbered findings

Each finding is a claim followed by the output behind it. Read the claim, open the output, and check that you can see the claim there before accepting it.

  1. Edges equal their formula in stability. Raw and first-order edges differed by -0.000117 to 0.000039 in intraclass correlation across all cells and groups (Table 6).
  2. Single-sample edges are unreliable over visits. Every group’s raw intraclass correlation lay between 0.069 to 0.225 (Table 3).
  3. Stable interferon makes interferon edges more stable, but cross pairs too. Interferon pairs went from 0.069 (no stable IFN) to 0.144 (measured) and 0.225 (very stable); cross pairs from 0.075 to 0.128 and 0.161, so the pre-registered excess was 0.016 (MCSE 0.0009) and 0.064 (MCSE 0.0015) (clauses 1(a), 2(a) fail).
  4. The fix removes the interferon part and keeps a real personal module. Fixed excess 0.0019 to 0.0068; in cell 4 (IFN stability 0.55, personal module 0.25, 6 visits) the fixed module excess was 0.019 (MCSE 0.0007) against 0.001 (MCSE 0.0008) raw (clauses 3(a), 3(b)).
  5. Identification comes mostly from the person’s gene levels. On all pairs, 0.261 (MCSE 0.0028) of people were identified raw and 0.275 (MCSE 0.0027) after the fix; on interferon pairs the fix changed it by 0.004 (MCSE 0.0014) (Table 4; clause 2(b) fail).
  6. Edges do not predict the next visit’s activity. Concordances sat near 0.48 and edges added -0.0006 (MCSE 0.0009) over genes even when activity changed the module (Table 5).
  7. The known-answer checks hold (Table 2).

Proposal proposal.md, final 2026-11-16 (re-scope)
Authors as in DESCRIPTION, set by tools/authors.R before the final render
Written 2026-11-16
Status draft; section 3 completed after the verdict. The pregnancy spec is the record in git (git show c677b11:project-spec.md)

1. Question and why it matters

Question (one sentence): Over repeated blood samples of the same patient, how stable are her LIONESS edges, can they identify her, and do they predict her next disease activity, beyond her interferon level, her measured blood-cell counts, her gene levels, and the edges’ own first-order formula?

Why it matters: A personal network is a biomarker only if it is reproducible and carries something the cheap measures do not. If its stability is the person’s stable interferon level and her own gene levels, a user would measure those directly; if a corrected network keeps a stable personal part, that part is the candidate biomarker.

2. Mechanism we suspect

A LIONESS edge equals, to first order, \(r + z_{qi} z_{qj} - \tfrac{r}{2}(z_{qi}^2 + z_{qj}^2)\), so it carries the square of any factor that moves both genes. For a factor with within-person intraclass correlation \(\kappa\), the intraclass correlation of \(F^2\) is \(\kappa^2\) (proposal section 4), so edges of genes sharing a stable factor look personal with no personal co-expression; a factor that changes between visits adds within-person noise. Each person’s own stable gene levels enter the product term too, so every edge is partly person-specific through levels alone. The gap is zero for a factor with \(\kappa = 0\) (the null cell) and grows with \(\kappa\). If the mechanism is wrong, partial-correlation edges would keep the factor-driven stability, or edges and their formula would differ.

3. Pilot

Code: pilot-d/pilot.R (Rscript pilot-d/pilot.R --reps <n>), then Rscript pilot-d/verdict.R; data description Rscript pilot-d/describe_data.R.

Pass rule: pilot-d/preregistration.md, section 2.

Verdict file: pilot-d/results/verdict.rds, after the run.

Plot: pilot-d/results/stability.png.

Status: piloted-close-call (2026-11-16), 200 replicates per cell, 6 cells, three cores, 2,714 seconds; verdict file pilot-d/results/verdict.rds. Numbers rounded from pilot-d/results/cell_summaries.rds.

  1. Does the effect exist? Edges equal their formula in stability (largest difference under 0.0001; 1(b) pass). Stable interferon raised the interferon pairs’ stability (from about 0.07 to 0.14 at the measured level, 0.22 when very stable), but cross pairs rose too, and the pre-registered excess was 0.064 at the stress level, below 0.15 (1(a) fail).
  2. Large enough at the measured level? No: excess 0.016 (2(a) fail); the fix changed identification on interferon pairs by 0.004 (2(b) fail).
  3. Is there a fix? Yes: the fixed excess was 0.002 to 0.007 (3(a) pass), and the fix kept a real personal module (3(b) pass). Edges did not predict the next visit’s activity (concordance near 0.48; 3(c) fail in cell 6). Single-sample edges were unreliable over visits (intraclass correlation 0.07 to 0.22).

4. ADEMP skeleton

Aims. (1) How much of the stability of LIONESS edges over repeated samples comes from a stable shared factor? (2) Does a person’s network identify her, and is that identification the factor? (3) Do partial-correlation edges remove the factor’s part and keep a real personal network? (4) Do edges predict the next visit’s activity beyond the genes, and do they equal their formula throughout?

Data-generating mechanisms.

  • Factors varied: the IFN factor’s within-person intraclass correlation \(\kappa_F\) (0, 0.55 as measured, 0.9); a real personal module (\(\tau\) 0 or 0.25); visits per person (6, the GSE65391 median, or 3); whether activity changes the module.
  • Factors fixed, and why: 131 people (the GSE65391 children with two or more visits); 50 genes and the loadings of the first project; the cell-mix factor’s intraclass correlation 0.45 (measured 0.41 and 0.48) and activity’s 0.39; person-specific gene levels of variance 0.5 (people differ in level); normal noise.
  • A cell where the answer is known: the null cell, with no stable factor and no personal module.

Estimands. The intraclass correlation of each edge over visits; the excess of the factor pairs’ intraclass correlation over that of cross pairs (one factor gene, one module gene), which share the person-level gene effects but not the squared factor; fingerprinting accuracy; the concordance of next-visit activity predictions.

Methods compared. Raw LIONESS edges, first-order edges, partial-correlation LIONESS edges given the IFN score and the observed cell-mix factor; for prediction, \(R_0\), \(R_1\), E1, F1, N1 as in the first project, Gaussian elastic net, folds by person.

Performance measures. Mean intraclass correlation by pair group; fingerprinting accuracy; concordance; each with its MCSE.

Replicates and Monte Carlo SE target. 200 per cell if the time box allows; the MCSE of a mean intraclass correlation over 105 pairs is then well under 0.01.

5. Application

Dataset: GSE65391 (Banchereau et al. (2016)), GEO; the series matrix and the GPL10558 table in data/raw/, fetched by analysis/00_download.R, not committed.

Comparison: within each of the 131 children with two or more visits; 897 visits; the authors’ training (91 children) and test (40) split as a second check.

What to show: how much of a child’s network stability and identifiability is her interferon level, her cell mix, and her gene levels, and whether corrected networks predict her next disease activity.

Decisions log

This is the agent’s decisions.md for the pilot, read from the file when the document renders.

D0. The literature pass

The re-scope proposal’s prior-work section (proposal.md, section 5) and log/01-idea-review.md (re-scope section, 19 queries). Nothing read since.

D1. The status call: piloted-close-call, with both readings

Every clause the rule names as deciding passed: edges equal their first-order formula in stability (1(b)), the partial-correlation edges remove the IFN pairs’ excess stability (3(a)), and they keep a real personal module (3(b)). Clauses 1(a), 2(a), 2(b), and 3(c) in cell 6 failed. Values in pilot-d/results/verdict.rds.

  • The reading that passes. The paper’s three claims held in every cell with 200 replicates: LIONESS edges and their formula have the same stability to within \(10^{-4}\); the fix brings the IFN excess to zero; the fix keeps, and sharpens, a real personal module. The failed clauses are about size: the IFN excess was smaller than the thresholds set from the sketch, and edges carried no next-visit activity signal.
  • The reading that fails. At the IFN stability measured in GSE65391, IFN adds little stability that the cross pairs do not also carry (excess about 0.016), it barely changes identification (raw against fixed, about 0.004), and edges do not predict the next visit’s activity even when activity changes co-expression. The application would then show little IFN-driven “personal network” to remove, and no clinical prediction.

The agent’s reading: a pass for the method’s claims, a fail for a large IFN-driven stability artifact. What the pilot found instead (D2, D3) is a different and possibly more useful message: single-sample edges are unreliable over visits, and what stability they have is mostly the person’s own gene levels.

D2. Why the excess was small: noise and the cross pairs

Two reasons, both visible in cell_summaries.rds.

  • Edges are noisy. Every edge’s intraclass correlation was between about 0.07 and 0.22: a single-visit edge is dominated by the product of the visit’s noise terms, so the part that comes from \(F^2\) is a small share of its variance. The sketch’s \(\kappa^2\) multiplies that share; the thresholds (0.15, 0.05) were set without computing it, which was the agent’s error.
  • The cross pairs carry IFN too. An edge between an IFN gene and a module gene contains the product of the IFN factor and the person’s own level of the module gene, which is stable with intraclass correlation \(\kappa_F\). The cross pairs’ stability rose from about 0.075 (no stable IFN) to 0.128 (measured IFN stability), so subtracting them removes part of the IFN effect. Not judged, and reported: the IFN pairs’ own stability about doubled, from about 0.069 to 0.144, between those two cells.

The rule is not changed after the run; both points go to stage 3’s design if the user goes on.

D3. Edges are barely personal, and mostly through gene levels

Fingerprinting on all 990 pairs identified about a quarter of the people from one other visit (chance under 1%), with or without the fix, and slightly more after it; on the IFN or module pairs alone, about 5% to 8%. The person’s own gene levels (variance 0.5 in the simulation, as people differ in level) give every edge a stable part, which is why cross and module pairs are as stable as IFN pairs. A real personal module with person-to-person spread 0.25 raised its pairs’ stability by only about 0.01. So an edge’s “personal” content is mostly the person’s gene levels, which the genes themselves carry.

D4. Next-visit activity: no signal

Every model’s concordance sat near 0.48 in cells 1, 2, and 6, below 0.5 for the reason of pilot-b’s D3 (activity has a person-level part that grouped folds cannot learn). Edges added nothing over the genes (about -0.0006 in cell 6). A single-visit edge cannot carry a change of at most 0.2 in correlation at that visit.

D5. The run

200 replicates per cell, 2,714 seconds on three workers, one pass (run_info.rds, run.log). The pre-registration, the change of rule, the user’s acceptance, and both amendments were committed and pushed before the run.

D6. What was not done

  • No edge was computed on GSE65391 (only its description).
  • One reference choice (the whole cohort); one noise level; six visits.
  • The within-person version of the prediction.

Action items and limitations

Action items

  1. Decide the status. The rule gives piloted-close-call; both readings are in the decisions log (D1).
  2. Decide the paper’s message. The pilot points to the low reliability of single-sample edges, and to the person’s gene levels as the source of what stability they have (D2, D3), more than to an interferon-driven stability.
  3. Confirm the re-scope with the supervisor (the yellow item in the spec and proposal section 9).
  4. Verify the citations; Devlin et al. (1975) lacks its full text.

Limitations

  • Everything here is simulation; no edge of GSE65391 was computed.
  • The thresholds of clauses 1(a) and 2(a) were set from a sketch that ignored the noise share of the edge (D2).
  • The cross pairs carry part of the interferon effect, so the pre-registered excess understates it (D2).
  • One reference choice, equal visits, normal noise.

It asks three questions: does the effect exist, is it large enough at realistic sample sizes, and is there an obvious fix or diagnostic? The proposal (proposal.md) holds the pilot plan and its pass criteria.↩︎

  2. piloted-pass means all three pilot questions got a clear yes. piloted-fail means at least one clearly did not, so the project should not go on as proposed. piloted-close-call means at least one answer could be read either way, so the call is stated both ways: the reading that passes and the reading that fails.↩︎

  3. LIONESS (Linear Interpolation to Obtain Network Estimates for Single Samples) builds a network from all samples and again without one sample, and scales the difference to give that sample’s network.↩︎

  4. Interferons are signalling proteins of the immune system; many genes respond to them together, and their summed expression, the interferon score, is high in many patients with lupus.↩︎

  5. Systemic lupus erythematosus is an autoimmune disease that can affect skin, joints, kidneys, and blood, and often flares in pregnancy.↩︎

  6. The Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) is the public archive of the US National Center for Biotechnology Information for gene expression data; a series (GSE) holds one study’s samples.↩︎

  7. In cross-validation the data are split into folds, each model is fitted without one fold and scored on it, and the scores are pooled; here every sample of a woman is in the same fold, so a woman’s own samples never help predict each other.↩︎

  8. The elastic net is logistic regression with a penalty that shrinks coefficients and sets many to zero, so it can use more features than samples; glmnet is the R package that fits it.↩︎

  9. The concordance index is the share of pairs of visits with different activity in which the visit with higher activity gets the higher prediction; 0.5 is chance and 1 is perfect, and for a yes-or-no outcome it equals the AUC.↩︎

  10. The AI agent that ran the pilot, wrote the files this document is built from, and kept a log of its decisions.↩︎
